sections.html: Phenacogrammus cf. taeniatus is a relatively small tetra from the Congo, imported for the first time. It looks confusingly similar to Alestopetersius smykalai from Nigeria, but has a black longitudinal band that is either barely visible or intensely black depending on the mood.

Tetras from the Congo are a new fashion trend in the hobby. Many species arrive under invented names, so it is often difficult to decide which species it is. Unfortunately, the animals are quite expensive.

Phenacogrammus taeniatus is so far only known from Cameroon. The fish from the Congo may therefore be a scientifically still undescribed species, although all externally recognizable characteristics of the new import fit very well to P. taeniatus.

The black longitudinal band is either barely visible or intensely black, depending on the mood. The rapid colour change is due to the pigment cells contracting, making the colour almost invisible, or expanding, making the colour suddenly shine. In preserved specimens the band is very prominent because the pigment cells relax in death. The Congo tetras are large flocks of silver glittering open water species.

Males are recognizable by the anal fin shape; females have a "normal" triangular anal fin. The photographed male is fully sexually differentiated at a total length of 5-6 cm, so the species probably does not grow very large. It is not known whether this tetra will develop a beautiful mating dress like Phenacogrammus sp. "Fantastique".
